title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 41-43): Grothendieck is listing the data attached to a family of motives over a base S (a variety over Q, or over a number field) once one fixes the motivic Galois group G of the family. The page collects that list.

A) G is a (reductive?) linear algebraic group over Q, the motivic Galois group, possibly non-connected.

B) P is a principal G_S-bundle over S, i.e. a G-torsor over S ("sur G_S" must mean "sous G_S"). It carries an integrable connection. This is the de Rham realization: the torsor of tensor-compatible trivializations of the de Rham fibre functor, with its Gauss-Manin connection.

C) The Betti realization gives a reduction of the structure group of P^an_C from G^an_C to the discrete group G(Q). Concretely this is the G(Q)-torsor P~ of rational Betti frames, i.e. the horizontal frames for the connection, with a covering map p: P~ -> P^an_C -> P. Equivalently it is a monodromy representation Γ = π_1(S(C), ξ0) -> G(Q).

D) There is a holomorphic map f: P~ -> 𝒴_G. Here 𝒴_G is the space of Hodge structures on G, i.e. homomorphisms h: 𝕊 -> G_R, where 𝕊 is the Deligne torus Res_{C/R} G_m used on p.42. The map satisfies:
- equivariance: f(xg) = g^{-1} f(x) for g in G(Q);
- compatibility with the de Rham torsor B), i.e. the Hodge filtration torsor and Griffiths-type conditions;
- compatibility with the comparison map p.
This is a G-valued period map. On p.42 the same data are rewritten via a section q over the universal cover of S_C and a monodromy w.

E) An adelic, étale datum. The G(A_f)-torsor P~ ×^{G(Q)} G(A_f), defined a priori only over S^an_C, descends to S. Equivalently, Γ -> G(Q) -> G(A_f) factors through the arithmetic fundamental group π_1(S, ξ0) -> G(A_f). This must be compatible with G/G^0, the Artin-motive part (the margin of p.42 says A = finite adeles).

NB. If the data come from a category of motives M, then A), B), C) together with the single value f(ξ0) should determine all of D) and all of E). Here ξ0 is a point of P~ lying over the generic point of S.
- Reason: the Hodge reduction of P is algebraic, so it is fixed by its generic fibre.
- The Galois action is likewise fixed by the motive.
The bracket 'conditions peut-être superflues' qualifies this.

Open questions he writes down:
- What can be said about data that genuinely come from motives?
- Is there an analytic formula for the prolongation (continuation) of f?
- What are the relations between D) (Hodge / period datum) and E) (adelic Galois datum)? The bracket, possibly 'fonctions automorphes?', points at the arithmetic of automorphic functions.

Modern reading: this is the notion of a 'variation of motives with G-structure'. The triple G(Q), a G(R)-space 𝒴_G of h: 𝕊 -> G_R, and G(A_f) is precisely the shape of a Shimura datum, with Sh_K = G(Q)\X × G(A_f)/K. Such a family yields a map from S to such a double quotient, and the question 'relation between D) and E)' is the question of canonical models and Shimura reciprocity.
errors: 'fibré principal ... P sur G_S' should read 'sous G_S' (G_S-torsor over S).

ξ0 'au-dessus du point générique de S' is not literally meaningful on the analytic covering P~. It must mean either a very general point, or the scheme-theoretic generic point together with a complex embedding of the function field.

The NB is false without motivic origin. For an arbitrary variation of Hodge structure, the period map is not determined by its value at one point. Grothendieck flags this himself ('lorsqu'on sait que ... d'une cat. de motifs').
The condition 'compatible avec B)' is left vague. Griffiths transversality, i.e. that f be horizontal, is not stated explicitly.
Reductivity of G ('réductif?') is asserted with a question mark. It holds for the motivic group of pure motives but not for mixed ones.

ideas.what: Family of motives over S encoded as: a G-torsor with integrable connection (de Rham), a G(Q)-reduction of the analytic torsor (Betti), an equivariant holomorphic map to the space of h: 𝕊 -> G_R (Hodge), and a descent of the induced G(A_f)-torsor to S (étale). These are compatible realizations with G-structure.
ideas.modern_name: Variation of (motivic / Hodge) structure with G-structure; G-local systems with Hodge and ℓ-adic data; 'motives with G-structure'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Travaux de Shimura 1971; Variétés de Shimura 1979), Milne ('Shimura varieties and motives', 1994), Simpson / Pink for G-VHS

ideas.what: Hodge structure as a homomorphism from the Deligne torus 𝕊 to G_R (used on p.42), with the target space 𝒴_G of such h.
ideas.modern_name: Deligne torus / Mumford-Tate formalism; Shimura datum (G, X)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1971 (with Mumford 1966 using the circle group for Mumford-Tate groups)

ideas.what: Combining a G(Q)-equivariant period map with adelic G(A_f) data, and asking how the Hodge and Galois data relate, possibly via automorphic functions.
ideas.modern_name: Moduli interpretation of Shimura varieties; canonical models and Shimura reciprocity

ideas.what: For data of motivic origin, the Hodge and adelic data at one (generic) point determine them over all of S.
ideas.modern_name: Deligne's 'Principle B' for absolute Hodge cycles; rigidity / theorem of the fixed part; algebraicity of the Hodge filtration
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, 1982); Griffiths-Schmid, Deligne (Hodge II)

ideas.what: Reduction of the structure group of the analytic de Rham torsor to the discrete group G(Q) via horizontal frames (Betti comparison), and descent of the induced G(A_f)-torsor to the algebraic base S.
ideas.modern_name: Riemann-Hilbert correspondence with G-structure; arithmetic monodromy π_1^et(S) -> G(A_f)

missed.claim: Already in 1965 Grothendieck packages a family of motives into exactly the three ingredients of a Shimura datum: G(Q)-equivariant data, a period map to the space of h: 𝕊 -> G_R, and G(A_f)-adelic Galois data. He then explicitly asks for the relation between the Hodge and adelic parts, with a possible pointer to automorphic functions. This anticipates the motivic interpretation of Shimura varieties (Deligne 1971/79, Milne 1994), which is usually not traced back to Grothendieck's motivic Galois group notes.
missed.quote: E) Restriction de P~ ×^{G(Q)} G(A) à S ... Relations entre D) et E) ?? [Fonctions automorphes ?]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This bears on the history of the Langlands-Deligne motivic picture of Shimura varieties. It shows that the Tannakian motivic Galois group was conceived together with adelic and period-map moduli problems from the start.

missed.claim: He poses the question of an analytic continuation formula for the period map f determined by f(ξ0) and the connection. This is an explicit 'prolongation' of the G-valued period map from one point, which is left open.
missed.quote: Formule analytique de prolongement de f ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It relates to explicit period-map formulas: Picard-Fuchs solutions, nilpotent orbits, and transcendence of periods at special points. Also relevant is the Bakker-Klingler-Tsimerman algebraicity / o-minimal programme on period maps.

missed.claim: His expectation that motivic origin forces D) and E) to be determined by the datum at one generic point is a precursor of Deligne's Principle B. It also foreshadows the general expectation that the Hodge and ℓ-adic data of a motivic family are rigid.
missed.quote: La connaissance de A) B) C) et de f(ξ0) ... doit en principe permettre de reconstituer D) tout entier et E)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor historical precedence point for Principle B and absolute Hodge rigidity.

deep.surprise_reason: In a 1965 sketch, Grothendieck combines a Tannakian G-torsor, a Betti G(Q)-reduction, a period map to the space of homomorphisms from the Deligne torus 𝕊 to G_R, and an adelic G(A_f) descent, and asks how the Hodge and adelic data relate (possibly via automorphic functions). This is essentially the motivic shape of Shimura data years before Deligne's formalization. It is a sketch with question marks, not a result, so the surprise is notable but moderate.
transcription_corrections: Line B: 'P sur G_S' should most likely be read as 'P sous G_S' (principal G_S-bundle).
Line C: the arrow label is 'p', and 'd'où revêt.' is plausible; there is a scribbled-out symbol before P~.
Line E: 'G(𝒜)' (finite adeles, per p.42 margin) rather than G(𝔸); the following words read 'avec compatibilité relativement à G/G^0'.

The bracket in the NB seems to read '[lorsqu'on sait que tout provient d'une cat. de motifs M]'. The next line likely begins with something like 'pour les données provenant d'une cat. de motifs ?' rather than 'Quelles ...'.
The final bracket after 'Relations entre D) et E) ??' begins with a 'J'-like letter. 'Fonctions automorphes ?' is doubtful; it may be another phrase. Uncertain.
The boxed margin note is largely illegible. 'Quand G est ... [semi-simple / connexe?] ... il suffit de connaître la connexion de P, et il suffit de connaître P_S' remains conjectural.
